props.title: Death Bell
props.initialSlug: The ultimate exam: life or death.

sections.content: Death Bell launched a new wave of South Korean high school horror, blending the academic pressure cooker environment with brutal Saw-style (2004) death games. The film taps into very real anxieties about South Korea's intense educational system, where students face immense pressure to succeed. This psychological foundation elevates it beyond simple gore, similar to how Battle Royale (2000) used its deadly game premise to critique Japanese society. The claustrophobic school setting and competitive elements influenced later works like All of Us Are Dead (2022).

sections.content: South Korean horror consistently excels at mixing social commentary with genuine scares. Train to Busan (2016) used zombies to critique class division, while The Wailing (2016) explored cultural tensions through its supernatural story. Death Bell follows this tradition, using its deadly quiz show format to examine how academic pressure creates real monsters. The film's influence can be seen in later works like As the Gods Will (2014) and Alice in Borderland (2020), which similarly trap students in deadly games. SUBHEAD: Evolution of Asian School Horror

The school horror subgenre has deep roots in Asian cinema, starting with Japan's Suicide Club (2001) and evolving through films like Corpse Party (2015). These films reflect genuine societal concerns about youth pressure, bullying, and academic stress. Death Bell stands out for adding the game element, predating similar Western works like Exam (2009) and Bad Kids Go to Hell (2012). The film's success sparked a sequel and influenced the merger of school settings with survival game scenarios.
